subject: math
title: Grade 6 Improper Fractions and Mixed Numbers
seo_title: Grade 6 Improper Fractions and Mixed Numbers Worksheets: Free Math with Answer Key (BC Curriculum)
meta_desc: Free Grade 6 math worksheets on improper fractions and mixed numbers for the BC curriculum: bar and circle models, number lines, converting both ways, comparing and ordering, and word problems. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_sub: Improper to mixed: divide (7 ÷ 4 = 1 remainder 3). Mixed to improper: wholes × denominator + numerator (3 × 5 + 2 = 17). To compare, look at the wholes first: 17/6 = 2 5/6 < 3 2/5.
body_html:
Improper fractions

In an improper fraction, the numerator is greater than the denominator, so it is more than 1 whole. The denominator tells how many equal parts are in one whole.

Mixed numbers

A mixed number shows the same amount as wholes and a fraction less than 1. The bars above show 2 full wholes and 3 more fourths, so 114 = 2 34.

Improper fraction to mixed number

Divide the numerator by the denominator. The answer is the number of wholes. The remainder is the new numerator. The denominator does not change.

Example

Write 236 as a mixed number.

3 × 6 = 18, so there are 3 wholes. 23 − 18 = 5 sixths are left over.

Answer: 3 56

Mixed number to improper fraction

Multiply the wholes by the denominator, then add the numerator. Keep the same denominator.

Example

Write 3 25 as an improper fraction.

3 wholes = 3 × 5 = 15 fifths. Add 2 fifths: 15 + 2 = 17.

Answer: 175

Comparing and ordering

Change the numbers to mixed numbers and compare the wholes first. If the wholes are the same, compare the fraction parts with a common denominator. You can also write every number as an improper fraction with the same denominator.

Example

Which is greater: 73 or 2 14?

73 = 2 13. Both have 2 wholes. In twelfths, 13 = 412 and 14 = 312.

Answer: 73

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
74 = 1 37 (the numerator becomes the denominator)The parts are still fourths: 74 = 1 34
2 35 = 65 (2 × 3)Wholes × denominator, then add the numerator: 2 × 5 + 3 = 13, so 135
Counting all the parts in the model as the denominator: 1112The denominator is the parts in one whole: 114
Leaving a fraction part of 1 or more: 2 7474 = 1 34, so 2 74 = 3 34

faq.q: What do Grade 6 students learn about improper fractions and mixed numbers in BC?
faq.a: The BC Grade 6 math curriculum lists improper fractions and mixed numbers as a Number learning standard. Students model them with bars, circles and number lines, change one form into the other, and compare and order them.

faq.q: How do you change an improper fraction to a mixed number?
faq.a: Divide the numerator by the denominator. The quotient is the number of wholes and the remainder is the new numerator, while the denominator stays the same: 23/6 = 3 5/6. A common mistake is 7/4 = 1 3/7; the right answer is 1 3/4.

faq.q: How do you change a mixed number to an improper fraction?
faq.a: Multiply the whole number by the denominator, then add the numerator, and keep the same denominator. For 3 2/5, 3 × 5 + 2 = 17, so 3 2/5 = 17/5.

faq.q: How do you compare an improper fraction and a mixed number?
faq.a: Write both in the same form. For 7/3 and 2 1/4, 7/3 = 2 1/3; both have 2 wholes, and 1/3 = 4/12 is more than 1/4 = 3/12, so 7/3 is greater.

items.q: Each bar is 1 whole. There are 2 full bars and 3 fourths more. How many fourths are shaded?
items.e: The full bars are 2 × 4 = 8 fourths. Add the 3 shaded parts in the last bar: 8 + 3 = 11. So 2 wholes and 3 fourths = 114.

items.q: Ava walks 134 km in the Terry Fox Run. Write this distance as a mixed number.
items.e: 4 fourths make 1 km. 3 × 4 = 12, and 13 − 12 = 1 fourth is left over. So 134 km = 3 14 km.

items.q: Jasleen says 74 = 1 37. What is the correct mixed number?
items.e: Jasleen used the numerator 7 as the new denominator. The parts are still fourths. 4 fourths make 1 whole, with 3 fourths left over: 74 = 1 34.

items.q: Harjot says 3 25 = 65. What is the correct improper fraction?
items.e: Harjot multiplied 3 × 2. Instead, 3 wholes = 3 × 5 = 15 fifths. Add 2 fifths: 15 + 2 = 17. So 3 25 = 175.

items.q: A pizza is cut into 8 equal slices. At a class party, students eat 19 slices. How many pizzas do they eat?
items.e: 8 slices make 1 pizza. 2 × 8 = 16, and 19 − 16 = 3 slices are left. So 198 = 2 38 pizzas.

items.q: Liam needs 3 12 cups of flour for banana bread. He only has a 14 cup measure. How many times does he fill it?
items.e: Count in fourths. 3 cups = 3 × 4 = 12 fourths, and 12 cup = 24. 12 + 2 = 14. So 3 12 = 144.

items.q: A jug holds 2 34 L of water. Each cup holds 14 L. How many cups can Chloe fill?
items.e: 2 L = 2 × 4 = 8 fourths. Add 3 fourths: 8 + 3 = 11. So 2 34 = 114, which is 11 cups.

items.q: 3 friends share 7 sub sandwiches equally at a soccer tournament. How much does each friend get?
c: 37 of a sandwich
items.e: Each friend gets 7 ÷ 3 = 73 sandwiches. 2 × 3 = 6, with 1 third left over. So each friend gets 2 13 sandwiches.

items.q: 4 hikers on Grouse Mountain share 10 granola bars equally. How many bars does each hiker get?
c: 410 of a bar
items.e: Each hiker gets 10 ÷ 4 = 104 bars. 2 × 4 = 8, with 2 fourths left over: 2 24 = 2 12 bars.

items.q: Arjun hikes 2 34 km in Stanley Park. Mei hikes 113 km. Who hikes farther?
items.e: 113 = 3 23. Mei hikes more than 3 km, and Arjun hikes less than 3 km. So Mei hikes farther.

items.q: It rains 134 cm in Vancouver on Monday and 3 12 cm on Tuesday. Which day has more rain?
items.e: 134 = 3 14. Both are 3 and a part. 3 12 = 3 24, and 24 > 14. So Tuesday has more rain.

items.q: The BC Ferries trip from Horseshoe Bay to Nanaimo takes about 1 34 hours. Write this time as an improper fraction.
items.e: 1 hour = 4 fourths. Add 3 fourths: 4 + 3 = 7. So 1 34 hours = 74 hours.

items.q: Three hiking trails: Lynn Loop is 2 12 km, Cedar Trail is 94 km and Eagle Ridge is 2 23 km. Order them from shortest to longest.
c: Cedar Trail, Lynn Loop, Eagle Ridge
Cedar Trail, Eagle Ridge, Lynn Loop
Eagle Ridge, Lynn Loop, Cedar Trail
Lynn Loop, Cedar Trail, Eagle Ridge
items.e: Use twelfths for the fraction parts. 94 = 2 14 = 2 312, 2 12 = 2 612, 2 23 = 2 812. So the order is Cedar Trail, Lynn Loop, Eagle Ridge.

items.q: Muffin trays hold 6 muffins each. Simran bakes 4 56 trays of muffins for a bake sale. How many muffins is that?
items.e: 4 full trays = 4 × 6 = 24 muffins. 56 of a tray = 5 muffins. 24 + 5 = 29 muffins.

items.q: A Grade 6 class uses 23 L of paint for a mural. Each can holds 4 L. How many cans of paint is that, as a mixed number?
items.e: 23 ÷ 4: 5 × 4 = 20, and 23 − 20 = 3 L left over, which is 34 of a can. So it is 5 34 cans.

items.q: Kai cuts a cedar board into pieces that are each 13 m long. He makes 11 pieces with nothing left over. How long was the board?
items.e: 11 pieces of 13 m = 113 m. 3 × 3 = 9, and 11 − 9 = 2 thirds left over. So the board was 3 23 m long.
